scope: Development clients, not virtual newsroom employees. No CMS or product-user accounts.
prerequisites: Separate clone/checkout per client; preserve any existing local edits.
Git read/write credentials for the shared branch and a configured Git author identity.
Fetch machine board before selecting work. Never start until claim push is confirmed.
workflow: Read project.json and task-board.json. Filter active release and dependencies.
Claim explicit task and write scope; save returned lease token.
Fetch latest shared branch into client code checkout before starting; never force reset local changes.
Heartbeat before lease expires; stop publishing work when lease no longer valid.
Commit and integrate tested code into shared branch with ordinary fast-forward pushes; resolve concurrent changes deliberately.
Submit already-published commit SHA and check evidence while holding valid lease.
Independent reviewer verifies actual evidence and unchanged file scope, then completes or rejects.
Release advancement and docs publication remain separate coordinator decisions after all tasks and integration checks.
commands: Test run URL or recorded check result
current_warning: T100 and other unfinished 0.1 tasks contain local pending work. Example claim is a template and will be blocked until reconciliation.
atomicity: Task state commits modify only planning/task-board.json. Competing pushes are rejected by Git; client refetches and revalidates up to four times. No shared unlocked JSON file and no force push.
leases: Tokens fence expired workers; explicit file paths or directory paths ending slash are required. Lease expiry does not cancel a running OS process. Clients must stop stale work themselves.
conflict_recovery: On failure do not assume ownership; refetch board. New cache clones stay under ignored .test-tmp/task-clients and do not change working checkout.
security: No secrets in tasks/check evidence. A client ID is not verified identity. Direct Git writers can bypass protocol, so all collaborating clients must follow it.
